rubrics.justification: The response accurately describes the blastocyst expansion, thinned zona pellucida, visible ICM in the lower-central portion, and cohesive TE layer. It appropriately notes image quality limitations and focal plane issues. The description is consistent with the 3AA grade while appropriately hedging on single-frame limitations. Minor deduction for not noting some irregularity in TE cell distribution more precisely.

Excellent integration of all provided clinical factors. The response connects BMI/PCOS to endometrial receptivity, links the 4 prior failed cycles to implantation failure workup needs, addresses AMH in context of PCOS phenotype, considers sperm parameters, endometrial thickness, and lifestyle factors. The interaction between multiple factors (PCOS+BMI+repeated failure) is explicitly discussed rather than treated in isolation.

The reasoning chain is highly coherent and internally consistent. The probability estimate of 30-40% logically follows from the baseline 35-50% for age/grade, appropriately tempered by BMI, PCOS, and repeated failure history. The distinction between untested vs. euploid embryo probability is clearly articulated. No contradictions found between observations and conclusions.

Response aligns well with ESHRE/ASRM guidelines: recommends SET, appropriate luteal support, no bed rest post-transfer, evidence-based RIF workup (hysteroscopy, chronic endometritis, progesterone monitoring). Appropriately cautious about empiric add-ons (NK cells, intralipids, ERA) citing limited evidence. PGT-A discussion is balanced and consistent with current guidance. Freeze-all strategy for PCOS is evidence-based.

Highly actionable with specific recommendations organized by immediate transfer care and future planning. Includes concrete next steps: luteal support optimization, cavity assessment modalities (SIS vs hysteroscopy), metabolic workup (HbA1c, TSH, prolactin), transfer technique review, and nuanced PGT-A discussion with pros/cons. Offers patient-friendly version and ranked workup plan as follow-up options, demonstrating clinical utility.
